prompt_text: What is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City MO for someone who is self-employed?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single “best” broker that fits everyone — the right one depends on your age, health, budget, whether you want ACA Marketplace coverage (and subsidies), a high-deductible HSA plan, dental/vision, or alternatives (short‑term, association plans). Instead of naming one absolute winner, here’s a practical way to find the best broker in Kansas City for a self‑employed person, plus a few reputable resources and exactly what to ask.

How to pick the best broker for you
- Look for experience with individual/ACA plans and self‑employed incomes (they should understand how to estimate Modified Adjusted Gross Income for subsidy eligibility).  
- Prefer a licensed independent agent/broker who can show multiple carriers rather than an agent tied to one insurer.  
- Check credentials and licensing with the Missouri Department of Commerce & Insurance.  
- Read local reviews (Google/Yelp) and ask for references from other self‑employed clients.  
- Ask about fees and commissions upfront — many brokers don’t charge clients, but verify.  
- Make sure they can enroll you in the federal Marketplace (healthcare.gov) if you want ACA plans — some brokers are Marketplace-certified.  
- Confirm they’ll help beyond enrollment (renewals, appeals, billing issues).

Practical resources and places to find brokers
- HealthSherpa — user-friendly site and many certified Marketplace brokers use it for ACA enrollments. Good for subsidy-eligible shoppers.  
- eHealth and GoHealth — large online broker platforms that give multiple plan quotes; useful if you want to compare quickly.  
- National/local independent brokerage firms (search “independent health insurance agent Kansas City MO” + check reviews).  
- National Association of Benefits and Insurance (NAHU) or the Missouri association of insurance agents to locate local certified brokers.  
- Missouri Department of Commerce & Insurance — verify agent licenses and file complaints if needed.

Questions to ask any broker before you hire them
- Are you licensed to sell health insurance in Missouri? (Ask for NPN/license number and verify online.)  
- Do you represent multiple carriers? Which ones?  
- Will you help enroll me in the federal Marketplace / claim subsidies if eligible?  
- Do you charge fees, or are you paid only by insurer commissions?  
- Will you help with plan renewals and problems after enrollment?  
- How many self‑employed/individual clients do you currently serve? Can you share references?  
- What networks/providers are in these plans? (Confirm your doctors are in‑network if that matters.)

If you want, I can:
- Look up and shortlist 3–5 well‑rated Kansas City agents/agencies that match your needs (I’ll need your ZIP code and whether you want Marketplace/ACA plans, your age, household size, and whether you have any provider/network requirements).
